test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 29 Jan 2021 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which of the following Article of the Indian constitution defines the Money bill?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 110.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **money bill **has been defined in** Article 110 **of the Indian Constitution. 
 
• **Article 110(1)** provides certain** provisions for a bill to be a money bill. **
 
• **Article 110(2)** provides **reasons for a bill not to be considered a money bill. **
 
• **Article 110(3)** says the decision of the **Speaker of the House of the People** thereon shall be **final.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 115 -** It has provisions for the demand for an excess grant. The demand is made when the expenditure has been incurred after a financial year has expired.
 
• **Article 109 - **It says that a money bill can not be introduced in Rajya Sabha, also Rajya Sabha cannot reject or amend the Bill and must return it within 14 days. The Bill is deemed to have been passed by both Houses once passed by Lok Sabha. 
 
• **Article 113 - **It mandates that estimates of expenditure from the Consolidated Fund of India are included in the Annual Financial Statement.
